So the way I define things is thus:

A culture is a collection of ideas that is shared and maintained by a group of people. Ethics are internally imposed, morals are externally imposed, they are both guidelines or strategies to succeed within a culture.

To your question, having a link between morals and legality makes perfect sense. Every society has a culture, and the rules for thriving in one necessarily preclude thriving in the other. I don't want to miss the point that this is mostly a one way street, laws derived from morals make much more sense than morals derived from laws. Morals are most often general principles, laws can be complicated compromises based entirely on some temporary and unique circumstance.

Your anecdote of underage drinking could well be an excuse made by someone with little insight.
